revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Deon's Errands
revealWordProblem.text:
Deon runs errands in his neighborhood. The map shows the neighborhood on a coordinate plane, and the table gives the location of each place on his list.
Question: Deon walks from the Grocery to the Library, going straight east and then straight south. How far does he walk? Which two places on his list are farthest apart in the north-south direction, and by how much?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A neighborhood street map on a coordinate plane beside a table of locations: Bank at 1 and one-fourth, negative 1; Grocery at negative three-fourths, 0; Library at 0, negative three-fourths; Post Office at negative 1, 1 and one-fourth.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Grocery to Library: the Grocery is at (−¾, 0) and the Library is at (0, −¾). Going east changes only the x-coordinate, a distance of |−¾ − 0| = ¾ unit. Going south changes only the y-coordinate, a distance of |0 − (−¾)| = ¾ unit. Together Deon walks ¾ + ¾ = 1½ units. North-south: compare the y-coordinates — Bank −1, Grocery 0, Library −¾, Post Office 1¼. The greatest and least are the Post Office at 1¼ and the Bank at −1, and because they are on opposite sides of 0 you add the absolute values: 1¼ + 1 = 2¼ units apart.

questions.stem: What is the distance between (-4, 3) and (2, 3)?
questions.explanation: Both points have y = 3, so this is a horizontal distance. |2 - (-4)| = |2 + 4| = 6 units.
choiceFeedback: 2 is the difference of the sizes 4 and 2, but the points sit on OPPOSITE sides of zero. Count the units from -4 to 0, then from 0 to 2, and combine them.
It looks like you counted from -4 only as far as 0 and stopped there. The segment keeps going past the origin to x = 2, so there are more units to add on.
This is the distance you would get if the second point were at x = 4 instead of x = 2. Find 2 on the x-axis and count only that far.
hints: Both points have y = 3, so they sit on the same horizontal line — only the x-values differ.
Find the gap between x = -4 and x = 2. The path crosses zero, so add the two distances |-4| and |2|.
Count from -4 to 0 (that's 4 units), then from 0 to 2. Add the two parts together.
questions.explanationEs: Los dos puntos tienen y = 3, así que esta es una distancia horizontal. |2 - (-4)| = |2 + 4| = 6 unidades.
hintsEs: Ambos puntos tienen y = 3, así que están en la misma línea horizontal: solo cambian los valores de x.
Halla la distancia entre x = −4 y x = 2. El camino cruza el cero, así que suma las dos distancias |−4| y |2|.
Cuenta de −4 a 0 (son 4 unidades) y luego de 0 a 2. Suma las dos partes.

questions.stem: What is the distance between (5, -2) and (5, 4)?
questions.explanation: Both points have x = 5, so this is a vertical distance. |4 - (-2)| = |4 + 2| = 6 units.
choiceFeedback: 2 only counts part of the trip. The segment runs from y = -2 all the way up to y = 4 — the units below zero and above zero both count.
You counted the part above the x-axis, from 0 up to 4, but the segment starts below the axis at -2. Add the units under zero too.
It looks like you combined the x-coordinates (5 and 5) instead of the y-coordinates. The x-values match here, which is the clue that the segment is vertical — the y-values are what change.
hints: Both points share x = 5 — the segment is VERTICAL, so compare the y-values -2 and 4.
The path crosses zero: split it into a below-zero part and an above-zero part using absolute values.
From y = -2 up to 0 is 2 units; from 0 up to 4 is 4 more. Add the parts.
questions.explanationEs: Los dos puntos tienen x = 5, así que esta es una distancia vertical. |4 - (-2)| = |4 + 2| = 6 unidades.
hintsEs: Ambos puntos comparten x = 5: el segmento es VERTICAL, así que compara los valores de y, −2 y 4.
El camino cruza el cero: divídelo en una parte debajo de cero y otra arriba de cero usando valores absolutos.
De y = −2 hasta 0 son 2 unidades; de 0 hasta 4 son 4 más. Suma las partes.

questions.stem: A rectangle has vertices at (1, 1), (5, 1), (5, 4), (1, 4). What is its perimeter?
choiceFeedback: The rectangle has four sides, and this only accounts for the two horizontal ones. After doubling the width, add the two vertical sides as well.
You used the coordinates 5 and 5 as if they were the side lengths. A coordinate tells you where a corner sits, not how long a side is — subtract the two x-values and the two y-values first.
hints: Perimeter is the distance all the way around — you need the width AND the height first.
Width: subtract the x-values 5 and 1. Height: subtract the y-values 4 and 1. Then add all four sides.
Find 5 − 1 for the width and 4 − 1 for the height. Now double each and add — that covers all four sides.
questions.stemEs: Un rectángulo tiene vértices en (1, 1), (5, 1), (5, 4), (1, 4). ¿Cuál es su perímetro?
hintsEs: El perímetro es la distancia alrededor: primero necesitas el ancho Y la altura.
Ancho: resta los valores de x, 5 y 1. Altura: resta los valores de y, 4 y 1. Luego suma los cuatro lados.
Halla 5 − 1 para el ancho y 4 − 1 para la altura. Ahora duplica cada uno y suma: eso cubre los cuatro lados.

steps: 1. Same quadrant / Same sign: Subtract absolute values of differing coordinates
2. Different quadrants / Opposite signs: Add absolute values of differing coordinates
3. Distance represents length, so it is always positive
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Distance on the Coordinate Plane is subtracting the coordinates as if both points were on the same side of zero, instead of adding their absolute values when the points are on opposite sides. For example, to find the distance between (-6, 3) and (2, 3), a student might subtract 6 − 2 = 4, but since -6 and 2 are on opposite sides of zero, the absolute values must be added instead: |-6| + |2| = 6 + 2 = 8. The correct distance is 8 units, not 4. Before you submit, ask: 'Are these two points on opposite sides of zero — and if so, did I add the absolute values instead of subtracting?'

level3.prompt: A rectangle has vertices at (-4, -2), (3, -2), (3, 5), and (-4, 5). Find the length, width, perimeter, and area of the rectangle. Show your work using absolute value.
level3.sentenceFrame: The width is |___ - (___)| = ___ units. The height is |___ - (___)| = ___ units. The perimeter is 2(___ + ___) = ___ units. The area is ___ × ___ = ___ square units.
level3.hint: Use examples with specific coordinates to explain your thinking.
hints: Width uses the two x-values (-4 and 3); height uses the two y-values (-2 and 5). Each pair has opposite signs.
Use absolute value: width = |3 − (-4)| and height = |5 − (-2)|. Then perimeter = 2(w + h) and area = w × h.
Start with the width: |3 − (-4)| means 3 + 4. Work that out, then set up the height the same way.
level3.explanation: The width comes from the two x-values, |3 - (-4)| = 7, and the height comes from the two y-values, |5 - (-2)| = 7, so this rectangle is actually a square. That gives a perimeter of 2(7 + 7) = 28 units and an area of 7 × 7 = 49 square units.
level3.explanationEs: El ancho viene de los dos valores de x, |3 - (-4)| = 7, y la altura viene de los dos valores de y, |5 - (-2)| = 7, así que este rectángulo en realidad es un cuadrado. Eso da un perímetro de 2(7 + 7) = 28 unidades y un área de 7 × 7 = 49 unidades cuadradas.
hintsEs: El ancho usa los dos valores de x (-4 y 3); el alto usa los dos valores de y (-2 y 5). Cada par tiene signos opuestos.
Usa el valor absoluto: ancho = |3 − (-4)| y alto = |5 − (-2)|. Luego perímetro = 2(ancho + alto) y área = ancho × alto.
Empieza con el ancho: |3 − (-4)| significa 3 + 4. Resuélvelo y luego plantea la altura de la misma manera.
